overview: Fisher & Paykel Healthcare is a New Zealand-based designer, manufacturer and marketer of medical devices used in acute and chronic respiratory care, surgery and the treatment of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), selling in over 120 countries. The business is organised into two product groups: Hospital (invasive/noninvasive ventilation, nasal high flow therapy, anesthesia and surgical humidification) and Homecare (OSA masks and home respiratory support). FY2026 (year ended 31 March 2026) operating revenue was NZ$2.31 billion (Hospital 65%, Homecare 35%), with manufacturing concentrated in Auckland, New Zealand, Tijuana, Mexico, and a growing Guangzhou, China facility.

business_model.summary: Classic razor/razorblade model: durable hardware (flow generators, humidifiers, the F&P 950 and Airvo 3 systems) is placed with hospitals and homecare patients, then drives a much larger, recurring stream of single-patient-use consumables (breathing circuits, humidification chambers, OSA masks) that must be replaced regularly. Hospital hardware is ~10% of Hospital revenue with consumables ~90%; Homecare hardware is ~12% with consumables ~88% (FY2025 mix). Growth is driven less by market volume growth and more by actively 'changing clinical practice' — training clinicians to adopt nasal high flow and other therapies as standard of care, which is a multi-year, relationship-driven sales process defensible against low-cost entrants.
business_model.customer_type: B2B — hospitals, healthcare systems and home care/DME (durable medical equipment) providers; end-use by clinicians and patients but purchasing decisions made by institutional and distributor customers
business_model.geographic_mix: FY2026: North America ~48%, Europe ~21%, Asia Pacific ~27%, Other ~4% (approx., per FY2026 revenue-by-region chart); ~99% of operating revenue is generated in currencies other than NZD (USD ~50%, EUR ~19%, other ~29%, MXN/NZD ~1% each) while manufacturing costs are substantially NZD- and MXN-denominated, creating a structural revenue/cost currency mismatch

competitive_position.market_position: One of the leading global players in nasal high flow/humidified respiratory therapy (Optiflow/Airvo) with an estimated ~8 million patients treated with Optiflow in FY2026 alone and ~24 million patients treated across the portfolio; a top-3 global player in OSA/CPAP masks alongside ResMed and Philips, competing on comfort/fit differentiation (F&P Nova, Vitera, Evora, Solo) rather than scale; total addressable market estimated by the company at NZ$25bn+ and growing (Hospital ~150m+ patients, Homecare ~100m+ patients)

moat_factors.description: Nasal high flow therapy adoption is driven by a decade-plus programme of clinical trials, published guidelines (ACEP, NICE, GOLD, ESICM, ERS, SFMU, AARC among others cited in FY2026) and hospital-by-hospital protocol changes; once embedded into standard of care and hospital purchasing/formulary decisions, switching is slow and costly for competitors to dislodge

~900 US patents/applications as of FY2026 with an average remaining patent life of 10.1 years across the portfolio; history of enforcing IP against ResMed (2016-2019 global litigation, settled 2019) demonstrates willingness and capability to defend design moats
Large global installed base of hardware (Airvo/myAirvo systems, flow generators) creates recurring high-margin consumables demand independent of new hardware sales cycles

In-house design, R&D and manufacturing across NZ, Mexico and China supports quality control and a continuous-improvement cost programme, evidenced by 122bps of constant-currency gross margin improvement in FY2026 despite ~90bps of US tariff drag
Multi-decade relationships with intensive care, emergency medicine and sleep clinicians; company positions itself as a trusted clinical partner, not just a device vendor

weaknesses: Sub-scale relative to ResMed and Philips in overall respiratory/sleep device revenue, limiting negotiating leverage with large group purchasing organisations
High revenue concentration in a small number of therapy franchises (Optiflow/nasal high flow, OSA masks) versus more diversified device peers
No major presence in flow generator/CPAP device hardware to rival ResMed's AirSense platform — homecare hardware remains a smaller, lower-margin part of the mix
Heavy USD/EUR revenue vs NZD/MXN cost base structurally exposes reported earnings to FX volatility regardless of hedging

growth_drivers: Continued 'changing clinical practice' campaign expanding nasal high flow (Optiflow) into new applications — emergency department, COPD/GOLD guideline recommendation, post-operative and ICU/HDU use — even as reported US hospital respiratory admissions were described as 'apparently subdued' in FY2026, suggesting share/practice gains rather than pure market cyclicality

New OSA mask launches — F&P Nova Nasal rolled out to the US (Jan 2026) and Europe (H1 FY2026) following earlier launches elsewhere, alongside Vitera, Evora and Solo ranges, to grow share in the ~100m+ patient homecare TAM against ResMed/Philips
F&P 950 System and Airvo 3 hardware roll-out driving above-trend hardware growth (Hospital hardware +27% constant currency in FY2026) which seeds future consumables annuities
Anesthesia product adoption as a newer growth vector within Hospital

Capacity expansion: fifth East Tāmaki (Auckland) building under construction (opening 2027, +28,000 sqm), a planned second NZ campus at Karaka (rezoning decision expected later in CY2026), continued Tijuana, Mexico expansion and a growing Guangzhou, China manufacturing and commercial footprint intended to serve China's large and fast-growing market without displacing NZ/Mexico investment

Gross margin recovery programme: continuous improvement initiatives targeting a long-term ~65% constant-currency gross margin (FY2026 actual 63.7%, +122bps constant currency y/y) even while absorbing tariff headwinds
R&D intensity (~10% of revenue, $235.5m in FY2026, >$1.5bn cumulative over 10 years) funding a growing product pipeline across both divisions

Structural demographic tailwinds: aging population and rising prevalence of COPD (~4-10% of world population, ~400m people) and other chronic respiratory disease support the Homecare and home respiratory support TAM

business.description: Hospital revenue depends partly on respiratory illness admission volumes (flu/RSV/COVID-adjacent seasons); FY2026 grew despite 'apparently subdued' US/major-market respiratory admissions, but a normalisation or step-down in admissions could pressure consumables growth
ResMed and Philips (post-recall) are both aggressively investing in mask comfort/fit innovation; F&P must continue new product cadence (Nova, Vitera, Evora, Solo) to defend and grow share

Company explicitly flags product quality/patient safety as a top material risk; a prior product recall provision was large enough to be treated as an abnormal item excluded from FY2024 underlying NPAT for comparability purposes

History of costly multi-year global patent litigation with ResMed (2016-2019); while currently settled with no active suits identified, respiratory/OSA device IP remains contested territory industry-wide

financial.risk: FX mismatch between revenue and cost base
financial.description: ~99% of operating revenue is non-NZD (USD ~50%, EUR ~19-20%) while a majority of cost of sales and >50% of operating expenses are non-NZD but the profit is reported in NZD off a NZD-cost manufacturing base; despite an extensive multi-year hedging programme (USD cover stepping down from 90% in FY2027 to 5% by FY2031, EUR similarly), spot/hedge-rate movement created a NZ$14.6m unfavourable net profit swing in FY2026 alone

FY2026 capex (incl. land/buildings, plant/equipment, intangibles) was ~NZ$195m, guided toward ~NZ$225m, driven by the East Tāmaki fifth building and the second Karaka land parcel (NZ$43m paid in FY2026, final payment due Dec 2026); this is a multi-year step-up versus the historical run-rate that will pressure free cash flow before the new capacity generates revenue

financial.risk: Dividend payout growth outpacing near-term FCF
financial.description: Dividends paid grew 29% in FY2026 to NZ$252.3m against free cash flow of NZ$446.6m — currently well covered, but capex step-up and no Dividend Reinvestment Plan currently offered reduce the cash-flow buffer

regulatory.description: US tariffs contributed ~90bps of constant-currency gross margin drag in FY2026 (32bps in H1) on hospital products sourced from New Zealand; management guides to a further ~50bps net tariff/Middle East-conflict-related impact in FY2027, an explicit and recurring drag on the path to the 65% gross margin target

regulatory.risk: NZ Medical Products Bill / Patents Amendment Bill
regulatory.description: Company is actively engaging with NZ's Ministry of Health and Parliament on the proposed Medical Products Bill and Patents Amendment Bill, both of which could alter the domestic regulatory and IP environment for its core manufacturing base

Market access depends on maintaining product licences (FDA, EU MDR, China NMPA and others) across 120+ countries; regulatory delays can slow new product launches such as Nova Nasal's staggered US/Europe/APAC rollout

macro.risk: NZD/USD and NZD/EUR exchange rate volatility
macro.description: As the single largest identified swing factor in reported (vs constant-currency) earnings; a stronger NZD compresses reported margins and profit even when underlying constant-currency performance is strong

Chair's report explicitly cites 'ongoing trade tensions, tariffs and conflict in the Middle East' as reinforcing the importance of resilient, geographically diversified supply chains (NZ + Mexico + China)

macro.risk: Freight, resin and input cost inflation
macro.description: Petrochemical-derived resin, packaging and global freight are meaningful cost of sales inputs; a High-Dependency Unit-style macro/climate scenario in the company's own disclosures explicitly flags shipping/freight and resin cost inflation risk
Hospital capital equipment purchases (hardware) can be deferred in tighter public/private hospital budget environments even though consumables demand is comparatively resilient

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global respiratory care and OSA device markets continue to grow on aging demographics, rising chronic respiratory disease prevalence (COPD affects an estimated ~400m people worldwide) and continued clinical guideline support for nasal high flow therapy; company estimates a combined Hospital + Homecare addressable market of NZ$25bn+ and growing
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate — Hospital hardware sales have some capex cyclicality tied to hospital budgets, but the large consumables base (~90% of Hospital revenue, ~88% of Homecare revenue) is recurring and relatively defensive; COVID-19 (FY2021-22) caused a sharp hardware demand pull-forward followed by a multi-year consumables/utilisation normalisation that has now largely worked through the base, with FY2026 hardware growth (+27% CC in Hospital) again running well ahead of consumables (+16% CC), suggesting a fresh, organic (not COVID-related) hardware upgrade cycle
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct sensitivity (net cash position, minimal debt), but higher rates raise the discount rate applied to FPH's premium growth-stock multiple and increase relative attractiveness of yield alternatives on the NZX
key_input_costs: US import tariffs on NZ-sourced hospital product

recent_developments.event: FY2026 annual results: operating revenue NZ$2.31bn (+14% reported, +12% CC), NPAT NZ$468.5m (+24% reported, +28% CC), gross margin 63.7% (+122bps CC despite ~90bps US tariff drag), total dividend 52.0 cps (+22%); FY2027 guidance issued of operating revenue NZ$2.45-2.57bn and NPAT NZ$500-550m, with an estimated 50bps net tariff/Middle East-conflict gross margin headwind

Company upgraded FY2026 guidance mid-year: operating revenue raised to ~NZ$2.30bn (from NZ$2.17-2.27bn) and NPAT raised to ~NZ$450-470m (from NZ$410-460m), reflecting stronger-than-expected hospital hardware and consumables demand
F&P Nova Nasal OSA mask expanded into the United States following earlier launches in other markets
Anna Curzon appointed to the Board (filling the vacancy from Pip Greenwood's Sept-2025 retirement); Margie Apa (former CEO, Te Whatu Ora Health New Zealand) appointed as 'Future Director'

H1 FY2026 (six months to 30 Sep 2025) results: operating revenue surpassed NZ$1bn for the first half for the first time, at NZ$1.09bn (+14% reported, +12% CC); NPAT NZ$213.0m (+39% reported, +28% CC); gross margin 63.0% (+60bps CC, including 32bps US tariff impact); interim dividend 19.0 cps
F&P Nova Nasal mask launched in Europe; Board visited the Guangzhou, China manufacturing facility to review operations and expansion opportunities

Construction commenced/progressed on the fifth East Tāmaki, Auckland manufacturing/R&D building (28,000 sqm, expected to open 2027); rezoning application for the second Karaka, Auckland campus under review by Auckland Council with a decision expected in the second half of calendar 2026

US tariff policy on imports (including from Mexico and on NZ-sourced hospital products) increased FPH's cost base through FY2026 and is guided to continue into FY2027 at a reduced (~50bps) net rate as mitigation actions (pricing, sourcing, supply chain flexing) take effect

items.vs_prior: new guidance (first FY2027 guide, issued alongside FY2026 result)
items.notes: Implies ~6-11% reported growth over FY2026's NZ$2.31bn

items.target: Overall improvement in constant currency, net of an estimated 50 basis point tariff/Middle East-conflict headwind
items.vs_prior: continuation of improvement trend but a smaller net tariff drag than FY2026's ~90bps
items.notes: Company reiterates a longer-term structural gross margin target in the mid-60s% (approx. 65%) in constant currency, versus 63.7% actual in FY2026

items.vs_prior: raised in Feb-2026 from prior FY2026 guidance of revenue NZ$2.17-2.27bn and NPAT NZ$410-460m
items.notes: Actual FY2026 results (revenue NZ$2,308.4m, NPAT NZ$468.5m) landed within/at the top of the upgraded range

items.target: No explicit single-year FY2027 figure disclosed in the annual report; FY2026 capex plus land was ~NZ$195.2m and prior guidance for FY2026 capex was ~NZ$225m
items.notes: Continued spend expected on the fifth East Tāmaki building (opening 2027) and the final Karaka land payment due December 2026

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Lewis Gradon: 'The key now is to sustain that momentum – continuing to innovate, improve and work closely with our customers to create lasting value.' Management highlighted that hospital hardware and new-applications consumables growth occurred despite 'apparently subdued' US and other major-market respiratory hospital admissions, framing continued clinical-practice change (not just cyclical demand) as the primary growth engine. Chair Neville Mitchell flagged heightened significance of 'ongoing trade tensions, tariffs and conflict in the Middle East' for supply chain resilience, and reiterated that growth in China is intended to complement rather than replace ongoing NZ and Mexico investment.

bull_case: Durable razor/razorblade economics: ~90% of Hospital and ~88% of Homecare revenue is recurring consumables riding on a large and still-growing global hardware installed base, giving high revenue visibility and pricing power

Structural, multi-decade 'changing clinical practice' growth engine (new nasal high flow guidelines, new applications) that is largely independent of hospital admission cycles — FY2026 grew hardware +27% CC even against softer reported respiratory admissions

Clear, credible path to margin expansion: gross margin improved 122bps in constant currency in FY2026 despite ~90bps of US tariff drag, with a long-term ~65% constant-currency gross margin target still in view and FY2027 guided to further improvement

Strong balance sheet and cash generation (net cash NZ$401.3m at FY2026, gearing -22.8%, free cash flow NZ$446.6m) fully funding the capex supercycle (fifth East Tāmaki building, Karaka campus, Mexico/China expansion) without needing to raise capital

Geographically diversified, in-house manufacturing (NZ, Mexico, China) plus a deep patent portfolio (~900 US patents/applications, 10.1-year average remaining life) provide resilience against single-country tariff or supply-chain shocks and defend against low-cost competitors
bear_case: Persistently premium NZX valuation (one of the largest companies on the exchange by market cap) prices in years of above-market growth and margin recovery; any growth disappointment or delay in reaching the ~65% gross margin target risks a de-rating independent of underlying operating performance

Structural NZD-cost/USD-EUR-revenue mismatch means reported earnings and margins remain hostage to currency moves regardless of operational execution — FX swung FY2026 NPAT by an unfavourable NZ$14.6m even in a strong growth year, and hedge cover thins materially beyond FY2028-29

US tariff policy is an explicit, ongoing and only partially mitigated cost headwind (90bps FY2026, ~50bps guided for FY2027) with further escalation risk given the administration's continued use of tariffs and the company's meaningfully NZ- and Mexico-sourced manufacturing base

Heavy capex step-up (fifth East Tāmaki building, second Karaka campus, Mexico/China capacity) suppresses free cash flow conversion over the next several years before new capacity translates into incremental revenue, and land/construction cost overruns are a real execution risk

Competitive intensity from ResMed and a post-recall-recovering Philips Respironics in OSA masks, plus Vyaire/Getinge/Draeger in hospital respiratory, could compress FPH's share gains or force higher R&D/marketing spend to sustain new product cadence (Nova, Vitera, Evora, Solo rollouts)
